claims.text: The baseline PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst is a nanoscale solid solution with homogeneous elemental distribution.
The baseline catalyst has minimal intrinsic lattice strain.
A controlled annealing protocol can incrementally increase lattice strain in PtPdRhRuIrOs.
Overall composition can be kept constant across the annealing series.
Particle size can be kept constant across the annealing series.
Increasing lattice strain shifts the d-band center of PtPdRhRuIrOs.
A strain-induced d-band-center shift changes the adsorption energies of ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
The adsorption-energy changes lower the ethanol-oxidation onset potential.
The adsorption-energy changes increase catalytic current density.
Annealed samples will exhibit a measurable d-band-center shift relative to the unannealed baseline.
Annealed samples will have a lower onset potential and higher current density than the unannealed baseline.
In-situ XPS or XAS can evidence the proposed d-band-center shift.
X-ray diffraction can quantify the annealing-induced lattice strain.
The proposed effect holds under typical aqueous ethanol-oxidation temperatures, potentials, and reactant concentrations when strain is the only varied material property.
Complex multimetal interactions make the magnitude of the d-band shift and its correlation with performance uncertain.
Annealing-related compositional reordering may secondarily influence the outcome.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant d-band-center shift would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to observe either a lower onset potential or increased current density relative to the baseline would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: PtPdRhRuIrOs contains six named elements, but the uncertainty field calls it a seven-element system.
